mass_source: Early (1894) Velo curb weight, 280 kg (Wikipedia; The Motor Museum in Miniature)

steering_servo.note: Driver's grip on the handwheel. First full run used kp 150, kv 10: it lagged 5 degrees under the ~13 N m holding torque; raised to a firmer grip. The 40 N m hand-torque limit is unchanged.

assumptions: Mass split, centre of mass (rear engine) and inertia are estimates; no occupants.

tire.note: Solid rubber tyre: round crown (ellipsoid, 18 mm half-width) with vertical compliance of roughly 0.3-0.4 MN/m per wheel at these loads (assumed), i.e. a 0.02 s contact time constant. A flat 60 mm cylinder with the default 0.005 s contact (about 100 MN/m) chattered in cornering: edge-to-edge rocking, 16% of steps with no contact and load spikes of 2.6x weight. A separate full-width envelope, which never touches the road, keeps spoke clearance checks conservative.
